purpose: Five megatrends incl. physical climate change, 2026-2045: conditional structural bounds only. identified = quotable conditional on the run; directional = context, never a point estimate.
adapter_disclosures: PPP BASE: regional and world GDP are PPP in 2017 international dollars (world ~$158T in 2025). Growth rates and ratios are invariant to the deflator base; LEVELS are not comparable to market-exchange-rate or nominal-USD figures. A nominal-USD level question is NOT identified.

DEMOGRAPHY: the default fertility path follows Fernandez-Villaverde & Norrick (2026): world peak ~9.0B in 2054, 2100 ~7.5B (UN WPP Medium: 10.29B in 2084), a deliberate low-fertility choice (CLAUDE.md). Labour-force, dependency and growth readings are conditional on it; scenarios/un-wpp-medium.json gives the UN Medium view.

RATES: three real rates. capital.interestRate is the return on capital plus the debt premium (~7% in 2025, firms' cost of capital); capital.safeRate (~1%) is paid on public debt and capital.loanRate (~3%) on private bank debt. The safe rate follows trend growth and public debt (Holston-Laubach-Williams; Laubach 2009) and can be held down by financial repression (repressionGap). It is not a policy rate or a market yield. There is no term premium. Use CHANGES, never the level.
NO TRADE BLOCK: the macro model has no bilateral trade, tariffs, exchange rates or current accounts. Trade-volume and trade-composition questions are not representable; fossil-fuel CONSUMPTION is.
NO PRICE LEVEL: no CPI/PCE, no nominal anything, no asset prices. Nominal-GDP and inflation questions are not representable.

LABOUR SHARE: laborShare (world compensation / GDP, ~65% in 2025, not comparable to national-accounts or BLS levels) is endogenous to automation only: robot and AI worker-equivalents' income since 2025 is paid to capital (capital.automationIncomeToCapital). AI cognitive payoff is off by default (production.aiWorkerEquivalentPerTWh = 0), so the default path barely moves it. Use changes across runs.

FISCAL: public debt follows an exogenous structural primary deficit (capital.publicDeficitRate) plus a borrowed share of ageing costs, less a Bohn fiscal reaction; interest at the safe rate accumulates into the debt. It is a world aggregate, not a US or any single-sovereign fiscal path.

CLIMATE: damages are a DICE-2023 / Howard-Sterner quadratic OUTPUT loss with regional multipliers (plus a tipping-point term in climate-cascade). The model has no public budget line for adaptation, disaster relief or insurance backstops, no insurance sector and no property market. Q3's fiscal quantity is therefore NOT in the model; only the size of the output loss is.

COVERAGE (C4, Q6 growth leg): OECD-38 + China is read as us + oecd-ex-us + china. The region tables are calibrated to OECD aggregates, but the nine-region split cannot reproduce OECD-38 membership exactly; treat the reading as an OECD-core + China aggregate.
PER CAPITA: the adapter reports GDP and population growth separately. Per-capita growth = (1 + g_GDP) / (1 + g_pop) - 1.

Q5 is NOMINAL USD and names EU-27. The model's market-rate GDP is at CONSTANT 2025 prices and exchange rates (it understates converging economies), and EU-27 is not a model region (oecd-ex-us also holds Japan, UK, Canada, Korea, Mexico, Turkiye, Australia). Only the real-growth leg of the US + China share is readable, and only directionally.

C2/Q2: the model's safe rate is a WORLD real rate on public debt under an HLW-type closure (r* = c x trend growth + z, plus a public-debt term, less any repression). It is not the NY Fed HLW estimate for the US, euro area or Canada and has no short-vs-long distinction. Use the sign and size of changes across runs.

questions.label: World trade/GDP volume elasticity 2026-2045
questions.refusal: no trade block: the macro model has no exports, imports, tariffs, shipping or exchange rates

questions.label: Elasticity < 0.75 and digital + minerals share > 42%
questions.refusal: no trade block and no nominal trade values by product

questions.label: G7 short-term neutral real rate, 2036-2045 average
questions.note: world real safe rate under an HLW-type closure; changes across runs only, never the level

questions.label: G7 neutral real rate >= 2.00%, 2036-2045
questions.note: same reading as C2; the 2.00% threshold is on the NY Fed HLW composite, which the model does not produce

questions.label: IMF advanced-economy gross public debt 2045, % GDP
questions.note: WORLD public debt / world GDP at market exchange rates under an exogenous primary deficit; sign and size of the change only

questions.label: G7 on-budget climate fiscal cost >= 1.5% GDP/yr, 2040-2045
questions.note: GLOBAL climate damage as a share of GDP is an OUTPUT loss, not a public outlay, and is world not G7; it bounds the scale of the problem, nothing more

questions.label: >= 3 G7 countries: robot/compute tax >= 2% GDP or formal YCC
questions.refusal: legislative and central-bank enactments; the model's repression rule is an assumption about a world aggregate, not evidence about any G7 country

questions.label: OECD + China real GDP per capita CAGR 2025->2045
questions.note: growth rates are deflator-invariant; conditional on the run, on the us + oecd-ex-us + china proxy and on the model's low-fertility demography; per capita = (1+g_GDP)/(1+g_pop) - 1

questions.label: US + China > 50% and EU-27 < 11.5% of world nominal GDP, 2045
questions.note: constant-2025-price market-rate shares: the real-growth leg only, no prices or exchange rates; EU-27 is not a model region

questions.label: 2045 regime: growth leg (g, 2035->2045)
questions.note: only g (OECD + China real GDP per capita CAGR 2035->2045) is identified; the inflation and sovereign-credit-event legs of regime C are not representable
